input.value: SchemaLocation pointing to a valid URI but schemaLoader returns a Schema whose getInputStream() returns null

cases.expected: JsonSchemaException thrown with message containing "Failed to load json schema from"
cases.description: When the schema loader returns a null InputStream the method should throw an IOException which is caught and re‑thrown as a JsonSchemaException.

input.value: SchemaLocation for a JSON schema where schemaLoader returns a non‑null InputStream but readTree throws IOException

cases.expected: JsonSchemaException thrown with cause being the original IOException
cases.description: If reading the InputStream fails, the catch block should wrap the IOException in a JsonSchemaException and preserve the cause.

input.value: SchemaLocation whose URI ends with .yaml and getFragment() returns null

cases.expected: JsonSchema instance returned (non‑null) created via doCreate with suppressSubSchemaRetrieval = true
cases.description: When the URI indicates a YAML document and there is no fragment, the method must read the stream as YAML, obtain the meta‑schema, create a ValidationContext and call doCreate with suppressSubSchemaRetrieval = true.

input.value: SchemaLocation whose URI ends with .json and getFragment() returns null

cases.expected: JsonSchema instance returned (non‑null) created via doCreate with suppressSubSchemaRetrieval = true
cases.description: When the document is JSON and has no fragment, the method must read the stream as JSON and follow the same path as the YAML case, but using InputFormat.JSON.

input.value: SchemaLocation pointing to a .yaml file with a non‑empty fragment (e.g. #/properties/name)

cases.expected: JsonSchema instance representing the sub‑schema referenced by the fragment (non‑null)
cases.description: When a fragment is present, the method must read the whole document, create a ValidationContext for the document, build the document schema via doCreate (suppressSubSchemaRetrieval = false) and finally return document.getRefSchema(fragment).

input.value: SchemaLocation pointing to a .json file with a fragment (e.g. #/definitions/address)

cases.expected: JsonSchema instance representing the referenced sub‑schema (non‑null)
cases.description: Same as the previous case but for a JSON document; verifies that the JSON branch and fragment handling work together.

input.value: SchemaLocation whose fragment object exists but getNameCount() returns 0

cases.expected: JsonSchema instance created via the "no fragment" path (suppressSubSchemaRetrieval = true)
cases.description: Even though a fragment object is present, a name count of 0 should be treated as no fragment, exercising the condition `(schemaUri.getFragment() == null) || (schemaUri.getFragment().getNameCount() == 0)`.

cases.expected: JsonSchemaException thrown with message containing "Failed to load json schema from" and cause being the original IOException
cases.description: When the underlying SchemaLoader cannot obtain a Schema object (throws IOException), getMappedSchema should catch the exception, log it and re‑throw a JsonSchemaException preserving the original cause.

group: Invalid YAML content causing parse exception

input.value: SchemaLocation pointing to a .yaml file; schemaLoader returns a non‑null InputStream whose content is not valid YAML

cases.expected: JsonSchemaException thrown with cause being the IOException (or JsonProcessingException) produced by readTree
cases.description: If readTree fails while parsing malformed YAML, the IOException is wrapped in a JsonSchemaException, verifying error handling for invalid YAML documents.

input.value: SchemaLocation whose URI ends with .YAML (uppercase) and getFragment() returns null

cases.expected: Non‑null JsonSchema instance returned; the stream is read with InputFormat.YAML
cases.description: The isYaml method should treat case‑insensitive extensions as YAML. The method must read the document as YAML and create the schema with suppressSubSchemaRetrieval = true.

input.value: SchemaLocation whose URI ends with .JSON (uppercase) and getFragment() returns null

cases.expected: Non‑null JsonSchema instance returned; the stream is read with InputFormat.JSON
cases.description: The isYaml method must not mistakenly treat .JSON as YAML; the document should be parsed as JSON and the schema created correctly.

input.value: SchemaLocation pointing to a valid .json file with fragment '#/nonexistent/path'

cases.expected: JsonSchemaException thrown with message indicating that the fragment could not be resolved
cases.description: When the fragment does not match any sub‑schema, document.getRefSchema(fragment) should fail, resulting in a JsonSchemaException. This verifies proper error reporting for unresolved $ref fragments.

input.value: SchemaLocation pointing to a valid .json file with fragment '#/' (root of the document)

cases.expected: JsonSchema instance identical to the document schema (non‑null)
cases.description: A fragment that points to the root should cause getRefSchema to return the same schema object that was created for the whole document.

input.value: SchemaLocation pointing to a valid .json file with no fragment

cases.expected: NullPointerException thrown (or JsonSchemaException if the implementation guards against null)
cases.description: Passing a null SchemaValidatorsConfig should cause the method to fail early (most likely NPE when config.getPathType() is called). This tests defensive handling of null configuration.

input.value: SchemaLocation whose URI ends with .yml and getFragment() returns null

cases.expected: Non‑null JsonSchema instance returned; the stream is read with InputFormat.YAML
cases.description: The isYaml method should treat both .yaml and .yml extensions as YAML files.

group: SchemaLocation with query string but no fragment

input.value: SchemaLocation whose URI is 'http://example.com/schema.json?version=1' and getFragment() returns null

cases.expected: Non‑null JsonSchema instance returned; query part is ignored for loading, fragment handling follows the no‑fragment path
cases.description: Ensures that a URI containing a query component does not interfere with fragment detection and schema loading.

input.value: SchemaLocation whose fragment string is exactly '#', resulting in a Path object with nameCount == 0

cases.expected: JsonSchema instance created via the "no fragment" path (suppressSubSchemaRetrieval = true)
cases.description: A fragment consisting solely of '#' should be treated as an empty fragment; the method must follow the same logic as when fragment is null.

cases.expected: NullPointerException thrown (thrown before any IO operation)
cases.description: Passing a null SchemaLocation should cause the method to dereference a null reference when calling schemaUri.getAbsoluteIri(), resulting in a NullPointerException.

input.value: SchemaLocation pointing to a valid .json file whose InputStream contains an empty document (e.g. "")

cases.expected: NullPointerException thrown when getMetaSchemaOrDefault is invoked with a null JsonNode
cases.description: An empty input stream causes readTree to return null. Subsequent call to getMetaSchemaOrDefault(schemaNode, config) receives a null schemaNode and throws a NullPointerException.

input.value: SchemaLocation pointing to a .json file whose content is {"$schema":"http://unknown/meta/schema"}

cases.expected: JsonSchemaException thrown with message indicating that the meta‑schema could not be resolved
cases.description: The $schema keyword references a meta‑schema URI that the factory does not know. getMetaSchemaOrDefault should fail and the method propagates a JsonSchemaException.

group: Invalid schema definition causing doCreate failure

input.value: SchemaLocation pointing to a .json file whose content is {"type":"not-a-valid-type"}

cases.expected: JsonSchemaException thrown from doCreate (invalid type keyword)
cases.description: The schema contains an illegal value for the "type" keyword. During doCreate the validator recognises the error and throws a JsonSchemaException, which propagates out of getMappedSchema.

input.value: SchemaLocation pointing to a valid .json file with fragment '#/properties[invalid]'

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException (or JsonSchemaException) thrown when document.getRefSchema attempts to resolve the malformed fragment
cases.description: The fragment string does not represent a valid JSON Pointer. getRefSchema should detect the malformed pointer and throw an exception (implementation may wrap it as IllegalArgumentException or JsonSchemaException).
